does: Turns pieces of fish in chermoula and leaves them in the fridge for a short while, so that the herbs, garlic, spices and lemon flavour the surface before the fish is cooked.
how: Pat the fish dry so that the marinade clings.
Spread the chermoula over every face of the pieces.
Cover and keep them in the fridge, not on the counter.
Leave them only for a short while. The lemon starts to turn the surface of the fish opaque if it is left much longer.

cues.text: Every piece is coated green, with no bare patches.
The fish stays firm and springy. Soft, chalky edges mean it was left too long.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the fish overnight, so that the lemon turns its surface soft and mushy.
Marinating on the counter in a warm kitchen.
mistakes.fix: Cover the dish and keep it in the fridge.

variant_of.differs: The marinade is a thick herb paste rather than a liquid, and fish is left in it only briefly because of the lemon.
